title: The buddy on Linux — two corrections

steps.path: Linux without the helper — replaces Q-2
steps.headline: Correction: the buddy DOES appear today, stuck. So what should someone see if they decline the helper?

options.label: Leave it exactly as it is today, and explain why it won't move (recommended)
options.summary: The buddy still appears and can still be pinned above other windows, same as now — nothing is taken away from anyone. One line in Settings explains that dragging needs the helper. Downside: people on other Linux desktops keep a buddy that sits in one spot forever, which is a bit unsatisfying but is what they already have.

options.label: Hide it instead, with a line in Settings saying why
options.summary: No stuck-looking buddy on screen; the Settings row explains the situation. Downside: this REMOVES something you can see today. Anyone using the buddy on a non-KDE Linux desktop would open the app after an update and find it gone. That is exactly the kind of unexplained change that is hard to trace back.

steps.path: People who already have the buddy on
steps.headline: You already have the buddy on, so there is no first switch-on left. When should you be offered the helper?

options.label: Next time you open the buddy's settings (recommended)
options.summary: Nothing interrupts you. The offer sits in the place you would go anyway if you were wondering why the buddy won't move. Downside: you might not go looking for a while, so dragging stays broken until you happen to open that popup.

options.label: A one-time prompt shortly after the update
options.summary: You find out immediately that the buddy can be dragged now. Downside: an unprompted dialog after an update, about a feature you did not ask about at that moment.

options.label: The buddy itself tells you — a small one-time bubble from the mascot
options.summary: It comes from the character rather than a system dialog, so it fits the buddy's personality and points at the thing it is about. Downside: it is a new kind of message the buddy has never sent before, and it needs building and reviewing on its own.
